Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 5. Free time
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: What's the weather like today?
- Materials: Weather cards, weather map, symbols, COSYmanuals 'impersonal it' and 'adjectives' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• ask and describe basic weather conditions
• use weather adjectives with impersonal it is

Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

weather — the state of the air outside. Example: The weather is sunny today.
hot — having a high temperature. Example: It is hot in summer.
cold — having a low temperature. Example: It is cold in winter.
sunny — with a lot of sun. Example: It is sunny today.
rainy — with a lot of rain. Example: It is rainy in April.
windy — with a lot of wind. Example: It is windy at the beach.
cloudy — with many clouds. Example: The sky is cloudy.
snow — soft white ice from the sky. Example: There is snow in the mountains.
warm — a little hot, comfortable. Example: It is warm in spring.
cool — a little cold, comfortable. Example: The evening is cool.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What's the weather like today? (asking about the weather)
• It's sunny. (describing the weather)
• It's cold today. (describing temperature)
• It's raining. (describing rain)
• It's windy. (describing wind)
• It's warm and nice. (describing pleasant weather)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the state of the air outside'?
Which word means 'having a high temperature'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Weather adjective stress and the /w/ sound

weather /ˈweðə/ — voiced th
sunny /ˈsʌni/ — stress the first syllable
rainy /ˈreɪni/ — long /eɪ/
windy /ˈwɪndi/ — short /ɪ/
Listen and repeat:
What's the weather like today? It's sunny and warm.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'it' to talk about weather, time, temperature, and distance.

Form:
Impersonal 'it': It is + adjective: It's cold. It's sunny. It's five o'clock. It's ten kilometres.

Examples:
• It is cold today.
• It's sunny in summer.
• It's five o'clock.
• It's ten kilometres to the city.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___ is sunny today.
___ is cold in winter.
___ is five o'clock.
Is ___ raining?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• It is ... (hot / cold / sunny / rainy) today.
• It is ... o'clock.
• It is ... in my city.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is the weather like today?
• What is the weather like in your favourite season?
• What time is it now?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about the weather with 'it is'.
• Write three sentences about time and temperature with 'it is'.
Reading: What's the weather like today?

What's the weather like today? It's sunny and warm in my city. In the north, it's cold and windy. In the east, it's cloudy and rainy. In the mountains, there is snow. I like sunny weather, but my sister likes cool weather. What's the weather like in your city?
What is the weather like in the writer's city?
Where is there snow?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What's the weather like today?
B: It's sunny and warm.
A: Is it windy?
B: No, it isn't. It's very nice.
A: What about tomorrow?
B: Tomorrow it's cloudy and rainy.
What is the weather like today?
What is the weather like tomorrow?
Speaking task: Ask your partner about the weather today and in their favourite season. Give a weather report for two cities.

• What's the weather like today?
• What is your favourite weather?
• What do you do on a rainy day?
• Is the weather different in the north and south of your country?
• Do you prefer hot or cool weather?
Role-play: You are a weather presenter. Give a short weather report for three cities.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about the weather today and tomorrow.
Model: Today it's ... Tomorrow it's ... In ... it's ...
